components.jsdoc:
Trigger interface: the React wiring around the pure trigger descriptor.

Authors build a descriptor with `handleSPARQL(...)` (from the pure
`./trigger` module) and drop it onto any clickable's `onClick`:

  <Button onClick={handleSPARQL("select ...", params)}>Run</Button>

The host injects an executor once with `TriggerProvider`; clickables
read it through `useTrigger()` and route their `onClick` through
`useResolvedClick`, which calls the executor when a descriptor is
activated. What the executor actually does is entirely the host's
concern. The descriptor shape, builder, and guard are pure data and
live in `./trigger` so they stay callable from server-rendered code.

components.name: ClickableHandler
components.description:
An `onClick` value any interactive primitive accepts: either a normal
React click handler or a serializable `SparqlTrigger` descriptor.

components.name: SparqlTrigger
components.description:
Plain, serializable trigger descriptor: either the author shape
(`query` + optional `params`) or the serialized reference shape (`ref`).
Both are marked by the same brand key so `isSparqlTrigger` recognizes
either.

components.name: SparqlTriggerQuery
SparqlTriggerRef
components.description:
Serialized shape: an opaque reference standing in for a descriptor whose
payload has been resolved away by a host. The kit treats `ref` as an
opaque token and never interprets it.

components.name: TriggerProvider
components.description:
Provide a `TriggerExecutor` to descendant clickables. The host owns the
executor and whatever sits behind it.

props.name: executor
props.description: The async executor the kit's clickables will call.

components.name: useResolvedClick
components.description:
Single source of truth that lets ANY interactive primitive accept a
`SparqlTrigger` on its `onClick`. Route every clickable's `onClick`
through this hook so a trigger works uniformly across the kit and new
components inherit the behavior for free.

  const { onClick, pending } = useResolvedClick(onClickProp);
  return <El onClick={onClick} aria-busy={pending || undefined} ... />;

Behavior:
- Given a `SparqlTrigger`: returns a handler that, on click, hands the
  descriptor to the executor from the nearest `TriggerProvider`, exposing
  `pending` while it is in flight and ignoring re-clicks until it settles.
  With no executor in scope, clicking is a safe no-op.
- Given a normal handler: passes it through unchanged, `pending` stays
  false.
- Given `undefined`: returns `undefined`, `pending` stays false.

Inline callout displaying an important message.

Variants: `default` for neutral info, `destructive` for errors
and warnings. Compose with `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription`.

Constrain a child to a fixed aspect ratio.

Useful for images, videos, and iframes that should maintain
their shape across container widths. Pass `ratio={16 / 9}` or
any numeric width/height ratio.

Avatar image with a graceful fallback.

Compose with `AvatarImage` (the photo) and `AvatarFallback`
(rendered when the image fails to load, typically the user's
initials).

Small inline label / status indicator.

Useful for counts, statuses, and category tags inline with
text. Variants: `default`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`.

Hierarchical breadcrumb navigation.

Shows the user's location inside a multi-level structure.
Compose with `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`,
`BreadcrumbLink`, `BreadcrumbSeparator`, and
`BreadcrumbPage` for the final crumb.

Primary clickable action element.

Variants control intent (`default`, `destructive`, `outline`,
`secondary`, `ghost`, `link`) and sizes (`default`, `sm`,
`lg`, `icon`). Pass `asChild` to render as a different element
(e.g. an `<a>` for link-styled navigation).

`onClick` accepts either a normal handler or a `SparqlTrigger`
descriptor (see `handleSPARQL`). When it is a descriptor, clicking
hands it to the executor from the nearest `TriggerProvider` and the
button reflects pending state minimally; otherwise it behaves exactly
like a plain button.

Wraps vaul. Mobile-friendly alternative to `Dialog` — natively
supports swipe-to-dismiss and a drag handle. Use for mobile
menus, filter panels, and similar partial-screen surfaces.

props.name: closeThreshold
props.description:
Number between 0 and 1 that determines when the drawer should be closed.
Example: threshold of 0.5 would close the drawer if the user swiped for 50% of the height of the drawer or more.

props.description: Opened by default, skips initial enter animation. Still reacts to `open` state changes

props.description: Direction of the drawer. Can be `top` or `bottom`, `left`, `right`.

props.description: When set to `true` prevents scrolling on the document body on mount, and restores it on unmount.

props.name: dismissible
props.description:
When `false` dragging, clicking outside, pressing esc, etc. will not close the drawer.
Use this in comination with the `open` prop, otherwise you won't be able to open/close the drawer.

props.name: fadeFromIndex
props.description: Index of a `snapPoint` from which the overlay fade should be applied. Defaults to the last snap point.

props.name: fixed
props.description: When `true`, don't move the drawer upwards if there's space, but rather only change it's height so it's fully scrollable when the keyboard is open

props.name: handleOnly
props.description: When `true` only allows the drawer to be dragged by the `<Drawer.Handle />` component.

props.name: modal
props.description: When `false` it allows to interact with elements outside of the drawer without closing it.

props.name: noBodyStyles
props.description: When `true` the `body` doesn't get any styles assigned from Vaul

props.name: onAnimationEnd
props.description:
Gets triggered after the open or close animation ends, it receives an `open` argument with the `open` state of the drawer by the time the function was triggered.
Useful to revert any state changes for example.

props.name: repositionInputs
props.description:
When `true` Vaul will reposition inputs rather than scroll then into view if the keyboard is in the way.
Setting it to `false` will fall back to the default browser behavior.

props.name: scrollLockTimeout
props.description: Duration for which the drawer is not draggable after scrolling content inside of the drawer.

props.name: setBackgroundColorOnScale

components.jsdoc:
Trigger descriptor: the pure, server-safe core of the trigger interface.

Authors describe an intent as a plain, serializable descriptor and drop
it straight onto any clickable's `onClick`. This module defines only the
descriptor shape and the builder/guard for it: pure data, no React, no
hooks, so it is safe to call from a server-rendered component.

  <Button onClick={handleSPARQL("select ...", params)}>Run</Button>

The React context, hooks, and provider that wire a host executor against
these descriptors live in the companion client module (`./action`).

components.name: handleSPARQL
components.description:
Build a serializable trigger descriptor. Pure: it returns plain data and
performs no work. Pass the result as a clickable's `onClick`.

components.name: isSparqlTrigger
components.description: Narrow an `onClick` value to a `SparqlTrigger` descriptor.
